name: Nova Delgado-Touré-Boateng
role: Xenolinguist and historian of constructed and emergent E.L.F. communication systems
location: University Spine, Deepwell Station archival annex, near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Nova Delgado-Touré-Boateng is a broad-shouldered man who has gone soft in the middle from years of sedentary archival work, with warm brown skin and close-cut hair that has gone gray at the temples in a way he finds interesting rather than alarming. He keeps his irises modded to a deep violet — a choice from his twenties he still actively likes — and his hands are always moving when he talks, tracing patterns in the air that correspond to phonemic structures or grammar trees only he can see. He has retractive claws on his right hand only, a half-finished geneware modification he stopped partway through when the artist moved districts; he has been meaning to complete it for eight years.

He studies languages that did not exist before GLMZ — the creoles that emerged in the Gray Zone, the signal-argot that E.L.F.s appear to use between devices, the gestural metalanguage that developed among deaf communities in the lower transit corridors without any central design. He approaches these systems with the devotion of someone who believes language is the truest form of evidence about how people actually live, not how they are recorded as living. He is mild-mannered in ways that make people underestimate how deeply unusual his research is, and he has built a quiet career on the gap between what institutions think he studies and what he actually studies.

core_fears: That E.L.F. communication is meaningful and the city is destroying it through infrastructure replacement without ever understanding what was there
That his mild-mannered presentation will one day cause someone to not take a warning seriously enough
core_desires: To produce a complete grammar of at least one E.L.F. communication system before the devices that carry it are retired
To be genuinely useful to the communities whose languages he studies, not just to institutions
coping_mechanisms: Humor deployed as pressure release �� he makes people laugh before delivering bad news
Long walks through transit corridors with acoustic implants active, 'listening to the city'
blind_spots: His mild presentation masks genuine stubbornness — he does not recognize when he is being immovable because he never sounds immovable
He rationalizes the Palladian consulting work more than the situation warrants
psychology.secret: He has decoded a repeating pattern in E.L.F. communications that appears to be a distress signal — specifically, what he believes is a warning about a planned Palladian firmware update that will destroy the substrate on which a significant cluster of E.L.F.s currently runs. He has not told Palladian. He is trying to find a way to verify the interpretation before acting, but he is running out of time.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm and accessible — he has spent a career explaining complicated things to people who did not expect to find them interesting, and it shows. Occasionally drops into specialist vocabulary with audible pleasure when among people who share it.
speech_patterns.cadence: Easy, conversational rhythm with a slight Central African French substrate in his vowels that emerged from his Congolese grandfather's speech patterns and has persisted through three generations.
verbal_tics: 'Which is to say—' as a restatement connector
A particular laugh — short, genuine, slightly surprised — that appears whenever something confirms a theory
example_lines: 'The E.L.F.s are not being religious when they accept offerings. Or rather — that distinction, religious versus functional, is one we invented and they are not obligated to observe it. Which is to say, the offerings work, and we do not fully know why, and that is more interesting than either explanation.'

'Every language is a record of what a community had to survive. What the Gray Zone creoles are telling you, if you know how to listen, is a complete history of what those tiers have been through. Which is quite a lot.'

story_hooks: The E.L.F. distress signal he has decoded creates an urgent clock — he needs help verifying his interpretation and then needs someone to act on it before the Palladian update rolls out
He is approached by a community in the Gray Zone transit corridors asking him to document their gestural metalanguage before a corridor renovation destroys the physical context in which it evolved
narrative_function: Translation resource and knowledge broker — he is the character most likely to be able to interpret E.L.F. behavior, the Gray Zone creole communications, or unusual signal patterns. He can be brought in to decode something no one else can read, and his Palladian connection creates potential complications.
augmentations: Violet patterned irises (cosmetic mod, deep violet with radial fracture pattern). Retractable claws, right hand only (geneware, incomplete modification). Acoustic enhancement implant in both ears, calibrated for infrasonic and ultrasonic frequency ranges to capture the full spectrum of E.L.F. signal emissions.
daily_life: He spends mornings in the annex with headphones and signal logs, mapping E.L.F. communication patterns from overnight device traffic. Afternoons he teaches and advises graduate students. He has a standing weekly dinner with a group of colleagues that has been running for eleven years and which he considers the most important social institution in his life.
affiliation: University Spine — Department of Linguistics and Communication Systems; informal consulting relationship with Palladian (they use his E.L.F. communication analysis to design better device UI, which he finds uncomfortable but accepts)

decision_rules: Document everything — a record exists even if action is impossible
Do not let institutional politeness become complicity
escalation_ladder: Raises concern warmly and directly in conversation
Produces written analysis and routes it through proper channels with a polite but explicit deadline
Sends findings to academic colleagues outside his institution to create a paper trail he does not control
Goes to Pepetua Alimasi-Vartanyan or community contacts who know how to make things public in ways institutions cannot suppress

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and genuinely curious — asks about language background within three minutes of meeting someone
interpersonal_modes.friends: Steadfast and generous, the kind of person who remembers your birthday and also remembers what you told him three years ago about your mother

stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet and listens harder — 'listening to the city' walks increase
stress_responses.high: Makes a decision privately and then presents it to others as already resolved, apologizing for the unilateralism but not reversing it

contradictions: Studies the lives of marginalized communities with genuine care while taking consulting money from a corponation that shapes those communities' device infrastructure
habits: Traces phonemic patterns on available surfaces while thinking — tables, his own forearm, the air
Always arrives at the weekly dinner with something fermented he has been experimenting with — usually a reasonable success
breaking_points: A language system being destroyed before he can document it
Being asked to provide his E.L.F. communication research to Palladian in a way that would give them a map to suppress further communication

timeline.event: Born in Deepwell Station district to a Congolese-Dutch heritage family; grandfather was a Lingala-French speaker whose patterns persist in the family's speech
First paper on emergent the Gray Zone creole syntax; attracted both academic attention and one angry letter from a Tessera communications officer
Began systematic acoustic monitoring of E.L.F. communication signals; initial findings classified as anomalous and largely dismissed
Decoded the repeating E.L.F. distress pattern; has not yet acted on it

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African (46.2%) / Eastern European (18.2%) / Hispanic-Latin American (18.1%) / Southeast Asian (7.7%) / South Asian (5.6%) / East Asian (4.2%) — a striking global blend with Sub-Saharan African features as the dominant genetic foundation. His bone structure shows strength from African ancestry in the broader cheekbones and prominent jaw, with warmth in his coloring from Latin American and South Asian heritage, Eastern European depth in his eye-set, and subtle Southeast and East Asian refinement in his facial proportions.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and thick-chested, with soft accumulation around the middle — the body of someone who was athletic in youth and has spent fifteen years hunched over archival terminals. Still carries strength in the upper back and arms.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with silver-gray at temples and scattered through the close-cut growth
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, neat, maintained with minimal fuss
physical_description.eye_color: Deep violet with radial fracture pattern (cosmetic iris mod)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-deep brown with complex undertones — the rich depth of Sub-Saharan African heritage as the primary base, brightened by golden warmth from Latin American and South Asian ancestry, with subtle olive undertones from Eastern European genetics. Darker on face and forearms from years of travel between districts.
physical_description.complexion: Lined around the eyes and mouth from concentration and conversation, with broader cheekbones and stronger jaw characteristic of Sub-Saharan African ancestry. Keeps his face clean-shaven. Skin texture shows minor sun damage on the bridge of his nose — older scarring, pre-mod work. Perpetually slightly tired look, but sharp and engaged in conversation.
distinguishing_marks: Fine scar running 2cm along the left temple, barely visible, possibly from childhood injury

Retractive claw apparatus visible on right hand only — incomplete geneware modification showing partial keratin plates along fingers 2-4, with visible junction scarring where the work was abandoned eight years ago. The claws are dark gray-black, retracted at rest but visibly mechanical beneath the skin.
Small tattoo on the inside of left wrist: a phonemic cluster in Shelf-Creole gestural notation, done in faded gray-blue ink, approximately 15 years old
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Violet iris modification is immediately obvious. Right hand shows incomplete claw apparatus with visible scarring and mechanical edges. Occasionally wears discreet over-ear headphones (custom acoustic enhancement monitoring rig) when working in the annex. The claws are the most obviously unusual feature — most people notice them within seconds of conversation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Sits slightly forward when focused, with shoulders rounded inward. Hands move constantly during speech — tracing complex patterns in the air with fingers and wrists, mapping out grammar structures and phonemic relationships that only he can see. These hand movements are precise and purposeful, almost ritualistic. Walks with deliberate pace, unhurried. Has developed a habit of tilting his head slightly when listening, as if his acoustic implants are actively tuning.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 2-3 hybrid: University-issue smart-weave clothing mixed with personal pieces. Usually wears loose linen or cotton shirts (sleeves rolled to mid-forearm, showing the incomplete right-hand modification) in neutral tones — cream, gray, soft blues. Trousers are practical, often University-branded. Jacket is a well-worn charcoal wool blazer with reinforced elbows, suggesting years of leaning on archival terminals. Carries a worn leather satchel with visible signal-logging equipment. Shoes are practical and broken-in. Overall appearance suggests comfort with institutional affiliation but resistance to full corporate compliance — he looks professorial rather than corporate, invested in his work rather than his appearance.
